definitions.gloss: leaving farmland fallow; resting agricultural land
definitions.explanation: The practice of leaving farmland uncultivated for a period to restore soil fertility, or the state of farmland being unused. Also refers to government-mandated reduction of rice production.

examples.japanese: {休耕|きゅうこう}{地|ち}が{増|ふ}えている。
{土壌|どじょう}を{休|やす}ませるために{一年間|いちねんかん}{休耕|きゅうこう}する。
examples.english: The land will lie fallow for one year to rest the soil.

examples.japanese: {高齢化|こうれいか}で{農家|のうか}が{減|へ}り、{休耕|きゅうこう}{田|でん}が{目立|めだ}つようになった。
examples.english: As the population ages and farmers decrease, fallow rice paddies have become conspicuous.

notes: Composed of {休|きゅう} (rest) + {耕|こう} (cultivate, plow). An agricultural term. Common collocations: {休耕|きゅうこう}{地|ち} (fallow land), {休耕|きゅうこう}{田|でん} (fallow rice paddy), {休耕|きゅうこう}{田|た}んぼ (fallow paddy field). In Japan, {休耕|きゅうこう}{田|でん} became widespread after the government's {減反|げんたん}{政策|せいさく} (rice acreage reduction policy) starting in 1970 to combat rice overproduction. Rural depopulation and aging farmers have further increased {休耕|きゅうこう}{地|ち}. Not to be confused with the homophone {急行|きゅうこう} (express train).
